open_points: CLOCK: 6.1.5 and 6.5 still say 'a game hour is 60 real seconds'. Decision of 24 Nov: 120 real seconds a game hour. Nothing in this file counts game time except hold times that are real seconds (hints 4 s, 12 s, 20 s, 30 s, 45 s, 60 s: all real, unchanged).

HINT TIMING: 6.5 says the quay hint comes after 4 s still; FirstMoments.cs has 10 s since 28 Oct (4 s before) and hints on hesitation. This file takes the blueprint's 4 s (newer than the C#); the 28 Oct ruling that hints are on hesitation not the clock is kept.

THE ONE USE KEY: 1.6.8 and 6.1.1 give one use key; the prototype had E, T and G for first, second and third things. T and G are dropped and the 'which?' prompt does the sharing. T is reused for Wait and G only in fights.
LEDGER KEY: 6.6 does not name it; L is the prototype's and is kept (chosen). Full stop opens Tom's reading.

PAD MAP: the blueprint names no pad button. The prototype's map (main.js round 6) is kept where its verb survives; every other pad button is chosen. Contexts differ (foot, car, fight, talk, ledger); within one context no two actions share a key or button (checked by script).
FIXED KEYS: 6.6 calls nine keys 'fixed' while AX-05 makes every action rebindable. Read as 'fixed defaults'. Only Esc/Menu (pause), Back and Leave are not rebindable (chosen).

THE WORD 'ROUND': the blueprint names the collection of payments 'a round' (2.17), but the content gate's aroundofdrinks rule catches 'a round'. No UI text uses it ('Collect the takings'); either the blueprint term or the gate pattern needs a ruling. See content-words.json.
REPORT KEY: 3.6.7 says 'a key' without naming it; F9 chosen (keyboard) and the pause menu (both devices); R3 in a talk on the pad.

NOTICE WORDING: the AI service's name and retention are not decided (PRIVACY-CHECK: 'checked when the services are chosen'). Placeholders {service_name} and {retention_text} with check_at_build true; defaults are for the browser build (Claude, made by Anthropic).
SPEAKER IDS: FirstMoments.cs uses older cast ids ('lena' is Sheila, 'rocco' is Ron); this file uses names.
PASTIMES: boxing club, snooker hall, fishing, pigeon loft (24 Nov) have prompts here (chosen); the blueprint chapters do not yet name them.
PRICES: prompts carry price_pence from PRICES-WAGES-1990.md; the prototype's 20p paper and 45p chips are superseded (25p, 1.60).
WAIT KEY: 7.11 says waiting is 'a key' without naming it; T chosen. The prototype passed the time on Z held, which 6.6 now gives to slow walking.
SAVE LABEL: 6.4 gives 'picture, day, hour, place and rung'; the rung words are the four rung names of 2.12.2. A rung 5 or later would need a word.

CREDITS: the Unreal-only rows (engine, characters, clothes) are marked unreal_only; the browser build ships only voices, type, assets and sound rows it truly uses. 10.4 does not say whether credits can be opened from the title; chosen yes.
DEFAULTS CHOSEN: subtitle box Half; chatter on; reduce flashing off; music volume 70; the rest 100. Subtitle steps 34, 39, 48 units.
ESC: Esc pauses everywhere (6.4, AX-10). Leave, Back, Ledger and map closing are on Backspace or the opening key; inside the pause menu Esc resumes.
PAD HOLDS: Use, held is its own key (F, LB); Tom's reading is a tap (D-pad up); map is R3; slow-walk toggle is L3; Front up on the pad sits in the manners pick.
FOV: ax.fov has built false until he rules on a field-of-view setting (AX-03).
999: calls to the police and ambulance are free; the generic phone box call is 10p.
The stitches prompt has no price yet in PRICES-WAGES-1990.md.
DRAIN: prompt.drain applies to a drain that map.json does not yet list.
The lead is Frank Nowak (canon, 24 Nov): the rung words and cue text use {first} and {called}; notes still say Tom (internal).

screen.title: Before you talk to anyone
body: The people of Meridian answer you in words made by an AI service while you play. It is {service_name}, and it works over the internet.
When you type your own words to someone, those words are sent to that service so it can make the reply. Nothing you type is sent until you choose below.
Why: only to make the replies. How long: {retention_text}
The game keeps no copy of what you typed. It remembers what was said in the story, the deed and not the text, unless you report a line.
Or play offline. Everyone then answers in lines written for the game, and nothing you type leaves this PC. The whole first hour can be played that way.
Either choice is fine. You can read this again, and change your mind, from the pause menu.
screen.footer: Report any line from the pause menu or with {report_key}.

privacy.title: Privacy and the AI replies

sections.head: What is sent
sections.text: Only what you type to a person when AI replies are on, and what the game needs to make that person answer in character (who they are, what they know, what has been said). Nothing is sent before you answer the notice.

sections.head: Why
sections.text: To make the replies. Nothing is sold and nothing is used to follow you.

sections.head: Who gets it
sections.text: At release, the makers' own server, which passes it on to {model_name} to write the reply. In the browser build, {service_name}. The makers receive a line only if you report it, and a crash report only if you say yes to one.

sections.head: What the game keeps
sections.text: The story's memory of what was said, in your save: the deed, not the words you typed. Typed words are not stored, unless you report a line.

sections.head: Offline play
sections.text: Switch to offline and nothing you type leaves this PC. People answer in written lines. The whole first hour plays that way.

sections.head: Crash reports
sections.text: A crash report is sent only if you say yes, and you can say no or never as easily as yes. It holds the game's version, the time, the last lines of the log and a short summary of the PC, with no serial number, machine name or user name. A report waiting on this PC is deleted after 30 days if never sent. A crash report goes to the makers.

crash_question.title: Send a crash report?
crash_question.text: The game stopped unexpectedly. A report would help mend it. It holds the game's version, the time, the last lines of the log and a short summary of this PC. It is kept for {crash_retention}. Nothing is sent unless you say yes.

ax_summary.text: Text size and contrast: all writing at least 24 units, up to twice the size, one plain face.
Subtitles on by default: size, box, speaker's name, street chatter.
Motion and comfort: shake, bob, blur, close-in, soft focus, flashing, field of view.
Audio: five volumes, mono, voices clear, soften loud noises, sound shown.
Input: every key and button can be changed, separate speeds, no mashing, holds as taps.
Menus: big still targets, Back goes one level, nothing destructive near Resume.
Saves: eight of your own and three that rotate, never losing the only one.
Pause when the window loses focus.
Nothing by colour alone; three colour-blind filters.

options.line: A darker panel behind the subtitle: none, half or full.

options.label: Show who is speaking
options.line: Puts the speaker's name before the line, for people you know by name.

options.label: Subtitles for street chatter
options.line: Words for voices in the street that are not to you. Turn off to keep only the people you speak to.

options.label: Camera shake
options.line: Turns off the shake from blows and cars.

options.label: Head bob
options.line: Turns off the bob of the view as Tom walks.

options.label: Motion blur
options.line: Blur when things move fast. Off to begin with.

options.label: Close-in on a blow
options.line: The brief camera step in when a blow lands. Turn off to keep the view steady.

options.label: Soft focus
options.line: The soft blur of things far from where you look.

options.label: Reduce flashing
options.line: Dims flashes from guns and lightning to fewer than three a second.
options.chosen_note: default off is chosen; AX-03 says the switch dims them; photosensitivity line shown once guns flash

options.label: Field of view
options.line: How wide the view is, from 75 to 100 degrees.
options.built_note: AX-03 keeps the view at 86 degrees until he rules on a setting; the record stays so the settings file and this list agree, but the control is not built and not shown.

options.label: Volume: everything
options.line: Sets the loudness of the whole game.
options.chosen_note: defaults for the five sliders are chosen

options.label: Volume: voices
options.line: Sets the loudness of people's voices.

options.label: Volume: effects
options.line: Sets the loudness of doors, blows, cars and the rest.

options.label: Volume: the street
options.line: Sets the loudness of the street, the gulls, the weather and the crowd.

options.label: Volume: music
options.line: Sets the loudness of the radio and any music.

options.label: Mono sound
options.line: Plays the same sound in both ears.

options.label: Voices clear
options.line: Lifts voices over the street by 6 decibels.

options.label: Soften loud noises
options.line: Holds gunshots and bangs down to the loudness of a slammed door.

options.label: Sound shown
options.line: Shows a short word at the edge of the screen for a loud noise you make, a quiet street, a shout or a car you hear. It shows what Tom hears, never what anyone knows.

options.label: Change the keys
options.line: Every action can be given another key, with a reset to the defaults.

options.label: Change the pad buttons
options.line: Every action can be given another button, with a reset to the defaults.

options.label: Mouse speed, across
options.line: How fast the view turns left and right with the mouse.

options.label: Mouse speed, up and down
options.line: How fast the view tilts with the mouse.

options.label: Stick speed, across
options.line: How fast the view turns left and right with the stick.

options.label: Stick speed, up and down
options.line: How fast the view tilts with the stick.

options.label: Mouse: up and down the other way
options.line: Reverses up and down for the mouse.

options.label: Stick: up and down the other way
options.line: Reverses up and down for the stick.

options.label: Holds as taps
options.line: Any action you must hold becomes one press to start and one to stop.

options.label: Aim help
options.line: Helps your aim once guns are in the game: off, light or strong.
options.chosen_note: appears only once guns exist; default off

options.label: Aiming dot
options.line: A small dot in the middle of the view when you aim.

options.label: Settings are kept
options.line: Every setting is remembered between games and survives an update. Not a switch; always so.

options.label: Saving
options.line: The game saves after every deed and when you quit, into three rotating slots, besides your own eight. Not a switch; always so.

options.label: Read menus aloud
options.line: Speaks each menu item and its value, and the Ledger's headings and lines, as you move to them.

options.label: Read prompts aloud
options.line: Also speaks the prompts in play, such as 'Go into Mickey's'.

options.label: Pause when the window loses focus
options.line: Pauses the game if you click away or switch windows.

options.label: Colour-blind filter
options.line: A colour filter for red-green (two kinds) or blue-yellow colour blindness. The game never relies on colour alone.

options.label: Never by colour alone
options.line: Every cue also has a shape, a word or the dark at the edge of the picture. Not a switch; always so.

options.label: Seeing outline
options.line: Draws a thin outline round the people you can see who are facing you. Off to begin with.

options.label: Slower fights
options.line: Fights start more slowly and only one man swings at a time.

options.label: Driving help
options.line: Eases the steering on keys and brakes harder.

options.label: Longer walks
options.line: Gives you half as long again to follow somebody who sets off.

options.label: Ledger stops the town
options.line: The town waits while the Ledger is open.

options.label: Hints again
options.line: Brings the hints back, one at a time.

display_options.note: The blueprint's PC list is complete; the browser build offers the rows with browser true. HDR and an upscaler are Unreal-only (8.3.1: 'where the engine has one').

options.label: Window
options.line: Windowed, borderless or full screen.
options.chosen_note: browser can offer Windowed and Full screen only

options.label: Window size
options.line: The picture's size, 21 to 9 included (3440 by 1440).

options.label: Smooth frames (V-sync)
options.line: Keeps the picture from tearing.
options.note: a browser always syncs to the screen

options.label: Frame limit
options.line: The most pictures a second the game will draw.

options.label: Picture quality
options.line: A preset for how much the game draws. Change any one below it yourself.
options.chosen_note: default Medium chosen; first launch picks one the PC can keep smooth

options.label: Picture scale
options.line: Draws the picture smaller or larger than the window, to suit the PC.

options.label: Upscaler
options.line: Draws smaller and sharpens it up, where the PC has one.

options.label: HDR
options.line: For screens that show it. Judged with Unreal.

options.label: Brightness
options.line: Lifts the picture overall. The night is never lifted past its floor.

options.label: Check this PC
options.line: Runs a short look at the town and says how smooth it is.

options.label: Show the change before you keep it
options.line: Shows a picture with the new settings and goes back by itself if you do not keep them.

options.label: Show key names
options.line: Show the key or button on each prompt.

sound_cues.rule: With the assist on, one short word at the screen's edge; none when off. It shows what Tom hears, never what anyone knows or thinks; no ring, gauge or meter. With only this assist on, every other measure is unchanged.
sound_cues.position: the screen's lower edge, left of the subtitles, never over them

words.sound_note: not a sound: fires when the street bed drops to its quiet state (sounds.json hour_states and mixes); no sound id

words.note: two-tone patrol siren (siren_patrol); the earlier word 'a police bell' is superseded
not one of the four cue types in 8.4.1; added for the ring that calls Tom; a third rule is needed to include it

sound_cues.words_note: 20 words. Every sound_id is a sound id in sounds.json (sound_list) or, for footsteps, a surface id in sounds.json footsteps.surfaces; 'the street goes quiet' has none (a state). The four cue types are the blueprint's; the words 'door forced', 'glass' and 'running on cobbles' are its examples; the rest are chosen. Dropped for lack of a sound: 'a drawer', 'a car stops'.

credits.check_note: Keep in step with THIRD-PARTY.md: a source added there is added here (tools/attribution-check.py). The browser build carries only what it ships; rows marked unreal_only are the Unreal build's.
credits.plays: after the ending, before play returns in the town; also from the title menu and the pause menu (chosen: 10.4 does not say whether it can be opened again)

lines.credit_line: A game set in a northern English seaside town, 1990.
The people of the town answer in words written as you play by an AI model, Claude, made by Anthropic.
lines.src: credits.json; the line applies when AI replies are on
